The strongest point in favor is the last 15 minutes: 502 buyers, $28k volume, net inflow of 113 SOL, and a 90% return. That suggests a lot of trading activity still going on.

But the curve data undercuts it. The FACTORY class, a bundle share of 1.0, and a top-3 share of 1.0 mean the early supply was concentrated in coordinated wallets, not organic demand. The first two minutes after graduation show 153 SOL bought by 21 buyers, with the top 5 buyers taking 99% of it and a sell-to-buy ratio near zero, which looks like a launch bot and insiders absorbing the float. A 21.7x return in 30 minutes, with the drawdown at zero, is the profile of a coin that hasn't yet had to face sellers. Recent sell volume of 62 SOL against 176 bought is real, but the sellers are small relative to the concentrated holders who can exit at will.

There is no solid case that demand will persist 30-60 minutes out. The base rate for factory coins is roughly 46% losses per trade, before fees of 1.4-5.1%. I would pass.
